cards.explanation: The answer is Peninnah. She's Elkanah's other wife, and she's the one with children. The verse says it flat out: “And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.” (1 Samuel 1:2). Hold onto that line, friends, because the whole story leans on it.

The answer is double. The text says “…to Hannah he would give a double portion, for he loved her…” (1 Samuel 1:5). Elkanah, Hannah's husband, gives portions to Peninnah and all her children, but Hannah gets a double portion. The text ties it to his love for her.

The answer is False. The double portion shows up in verse 5, but the reason given for the taunting is in verse 6: “Because the LORD had closed Hannah’s womb, her rival would provoke her viciously to taunt her.” The text doesn't link it to the portion. I think this part of the story hurts, so let's just read it plainly.

The answer is that she weeps and will not eat. The text says her rival “…taunted her until she wept and would not eat.” (1 Samuel 1:7). This went on year after year, every trip to the house of the LORD. I think this is one of the heavy spots in the story.

The answer is True. The text says, “In her bitter distress, Hannah prayed to the LORD and wept with many tears.” (1 Samuel 1:10). She brings all of it to the LORD, tears included. I think that's a tender moment.

The answer is that she will dedicate him to the LORD for life. Hannah says, “…then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life…” (1 Samuel 1:11). She asks for a son and promises him right back to the LORD. Hold onto that vow, friends.

The answer is True. Hannah's vow ends with “…and no razor shall ever touch his head.” (1 Samuel 1:11). It's part of what she promises, right alongside dedicating him to the LORD. She makes it in the same breath.

The answer is drunk. That's what Eli, the priest, thinks. The text says, “Hannah was praying in her heart, and though her lips were moving, her voice could not be heard. So Eli thought she was drunk” (1 Samuel 1:13). He saw moving lips and no sound, and he jumped to that. I've been guilty of jumping to conclusions over less.

The answer is that she's been pouring out her soul before the LORD. Hannah tells Eli, the priest, “I have not had any wine or strong drink, but I have poured out my soul before the LORD.” (1 Samuel 1:15). She tells him plainly what she's been doing, in answer to his accusation.

The answer is that Eli tells her to go in peace and says God may grant her request. Eli, the priest, says, “Go in peace… and may the God of Israel grant the petition you have asked of Him.” (1 Samuel 1:17). A few verses earlier he said, “Put away your wine!” (1 Samuel 1:14), so that's quite a turn. Hannah's explanation comes right before he says it.

The answer is True. After Eli, the priest, speaks to her, the text says, “Then she went on her way, and she began to eat, and her face was no longer downcast.” (1 Samuel 1:18). Back in verse 7 she wept and wouldn't eat, so this is a real change. She's carrying Eli's blessing out the door.

The answer is True. The text says, “…and the LORD remembered her.” (1 Samuel 1:19). Remembering her was exactly what Hannah asked for in her vow (1 Samuel 1:11). The prayer she poured out at Shiloh gets its answer back home in Ramah.

The answer is that she asked the LORD for him. Hannah names her son Samuel and says, “Because I have asked for him from the LORD.” (1 Samuel 1:20). Samuel is the boy she prayed for. The name carries her prayer.

The answer is weaned. Hannah tells her husband, Elkanah, “After the boy is weaned, I will take him to appear before the LORD…” (1 Samuel 1:22). She waits until then. I think she's taking her time with this baby, and I respect it.

The answer is False. Hannah tells her husband she will take the boy “…to appear before the LORD and to stay there permanently.” (1 Samuel 1:22). She isn't planning a round trip. She's keeping the promise she made in her vow.

The answer is that Elkanah tells her to do what she thinks best. Elkanah, her husband, says, “Do what you think is best… and stay here until you have weaned him. Only may the LORD confirm His word.” (1 Samuel 1:23). He leaves the timing with her and asks the LORD to confirm His word.

The answer is Eli. The text says, “And when they had slaughtered the bull, they brought the boy to Eli.” (1 Samuel 1:25). He's the priest Hannah met earlier, the one who told her to put away her wine. Now she's back with her answered prayer.

The answer is that the LORD gave her what she asked. Hannah tells Eli, “I prayed for this boy, and since the LORD has granted me what I asked of Him…” (1 Samuel 1:27). She credits the LORD for the answer. She doesn't take any of the credit herself.

The answer is that her heart rejoices in the LORD. Hannah prays, “My heart rejoices in the LORD…” (1 Samuel 2:1). This is the same woman who was in bitter distress at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1:10). Her song begins with joy.
The answer is that the LORD knows and weighs actions. Hannah says, “…for the LORD is a God who knows, and by Him actions are weighed.” (1 Samuel 2:3). So proud boasting is up against a God who knows.

The answer is that she gives birth to seven. The line is “The barren woman gives birth to seven…” (1 Samuel 2:5). Hannah says it in her prayer. I think it echoes her own story, but that's my guess, not the text's.

The answer is True. Hannah prays, “The LORD sends poverty and wealth; He humbles and He exalts.” (1 Samuel 2:7). Both are in her prayer, and the LORD is the one doing the sending. That's the whole line.

The answer is a throne of honor among princes. The prayer says, “He seats them among princes and bestows on them a throne of honor.” (1 Samuel 2:8). From the dust and the ash heap to a seat among princes. That's quite a lift.

The answer is False. Hannah prays, “for by his own strength shall no man prevail.” (1 Samuel 2:9). So her prayer says the opposite of the statement. Just before that, she says, “He guards the steps of His faithful ones…” (1 Samuel 2:9). I spent years in a junk drawer trying to get out on my own strength, friends, and let me tell you, that drawer did not budge.

The answer is that they will be shattered. Hannah prays, “Those who oppose the LORD will be shattered. He will thunder from heaven against them.” (1 Samuel 2:10). It's a serious line, and the text just states it.

The answer is that Samuel is ministering to the LORD before Eli. The text says, “Then Elkanah went home to Ramah, but the boy began ministering to the LORD before Eli the priest.” (1 Samuel 2:11). Samuel is Hannah's little boy, and he stays at Shiloh. She kept her vow.
